item.title: SA: Vusi Mahlasela announces new album
item.description: South African music veteran Vusi Mahlasela, widely regarded as “The Voice,” is preparing a major comeback with a new album scheduled for release in February 2026. Known for his distinctive blend of folk, jazz, and African rhythms, Mahlasela has been a prominent figure in the nation’s music scene for over three decades. item.title: Merlin signs AI licensing partnership with Udio
item.description: Merlin, the digital music licensing organisation representing independent record labels and distributors, has entered into a new partnership with AI music creation platform Udio, establishing a licensed framework for the use of independent music in artificial intelligence training. Under the agreement, Udio will train new AI models using music licensed from participating Merlin members. item.title: MaxNote Media acquires Eden Groove Sounds to boost African electronic music
item.description: South African independent music company MaxNote Media has acquired Eden Groove Sounds as part of a strategy to increase its release output and strengthen pathways for African electronic music into international markets. The acquisition is intended to expand MaxNote Media’s release pipeline while positioning Eden Groove Sounds as a dedicated imprint focused on long-term artist development and catalogue growth. item.title: Open call: Mahindra Fusion Fest 2026 in SA
item.description: Mahindra Fusion Fest 2026 has opened a nationwide call for entries, inviting creatives across South Africa to participate in a talent competition spanning music, fashion and art. The open call forms part of the festival’s broader programme and is positioned as a platform for emerging and independent creators to showcase their work in front of a national audience. item.description: Mahindra Fusion Fest 2026 will return to the SunBet Arena at Time Square in Pretoria this March, with organisers confirming an expanded programme that combines live music, fashion and visual art in a single, curated event. Following its inaugural edition, the festival is set to once again position itself as a platform for collaboration across creative disciplines. item.title: Ndlovu Youth Choir announces 2026 SA tour dates
item.description: The Ndlovu Youth Choir has announced a South African tour for 2026, marking its first major local run since achieving international recognition as finalists on America’s Got Talent in 2019. The tour will open at Cape Town’s Artscape Opera House, with performances scheduled from 5 to 8 February 2026, before concluding at the Teatro at Montecasino in Johannesburg from 30 July to 2 August 2026. item.title: Nasty C releases Head Up 2.0 visuals featuring Soweto Gospel Choir
item.description: South African rapper Nasty C has released the music video for ‘Head Up 2.0’, a new version of his track created in collaboration with the Soweto Gospel Choir. The video marks his first major release of the year and brings together hip hop and choral music in a joint visual and musical project. ‘Head Up 2.0’ revisits a song that Nasty C says developed over several years, shaped by personal reflection and periods of uncertainty. item.title: Open call: 2026 Harare International Fringe Festival
item.description: The organisers of the Harare International Fringe Festival have opened applications for the third edition of the event, scheduled to take place from 17 to 20 September 2026 in Harare, Zimbabwe. Formerly known as the One Hander International Theatre Festival (OHIT), the festival is inviting theatre artists, from various disciplines including music, from Zimbabwe and abroad to submit original productions for consideration. item.title: Open call: The Music Imbizo 2026 speakers and panellists
item.description: The Music Imbizo has opened applications for speakers and panellists for its 2026 edition, scheduled to take place from 26 August to Saturday 29 August 2026. item.title: The structural challenge facing African culture
item.description: Across Africa, cultural visibility is no longer a marginal phenomenon. This shift has not resulted from a sudden awakening or a single breakthrough, but from the speed and reach with which music, film and live digital culture now circulate. Music crosses borders almost instantly, films travel more easily beyond their countries of origin, and audiences gather around live digital moments in ways that increasingly resemble the shared rituals of concerts, cinemas and festivals.
